title: Cross-workload FP8 stability matrix and calibration orbiter
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reproducible, cross-workload FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) enablement flow for Hopper GPUs driven by a calibration orchestrator ("orbiter") that evaluates stability across representative production workloads. The orbiter will: 1) run deterministic calibration passes on canonical dataset suites (chat, summarization, code, retrieval-augmented prompts), 2) build a stability matrix per-layer and per-op comparing E4M3/E5M2 profiles and int8 baselines, 3) drive telemetry gating thresholds for canary activation, and 4) schedule shadow canaries and progressive rollouts. Goal is to reduce manual tuning, quantify accuracy regression risk, and automate safe activation/rollback recommendations.
acceptance_criteria: Orbiter service can run full calibration sweep for a model family on Hopper and produce a stability matrix JSON artifact within defined SLAs
Stability matrix includes per-layer sensitivity, worst-case delta on evaluation metrics, and suggested profile (E4M3 or E5M2) with a confidence score
Canary gating rules derived from orbiter outputs are consumable by runtime rollouts and prevent FP8 activation when regression risk > 1% measured on golden-suite prompts
Shadow canary runs are automated and produce telemetry dashboards in Console with token-level cost/latency and accuracy deltas
End-to-end pipeline documented and reproducible from a single orchestration job; PR merged to runtime and orbiter code reviewed
Automated rollback policy triggers when live regression metric breaches threshold for two consecutive windows
test_plan: Create canonical workload suite (n=120 prompts per workload class) and baseline with FP16 and INT8
Run orbiter calibration in CI for a subset (smoke) and nightly for full matrix; validate outputs against golden seeds
Inject synthetic drift (noise, tokenization edge cases) to ensure hysteresis prevents flapping activations
Shadow canary: route 0.5% of traffic with FP8 tensors to compute divergence metrics and compare to production responses
End-to-end integration test with Console dashboard flags and alerting configured in PagerDuty
implementation_notes: Orbiter is a stateless orchestration service that schedules calibration jobs on dedicated GPU pools and aggregates telemetry into a stability matrix
Calibration jobs must run deterministic sampling (fixed RNG seeds, fixed batched ordering) to ensure comparability across runs
Per-layer scaling and a histogram of activation quantiles will be emitted; we will use median+tail metrics to pick E4M3 vs E5M2
Use golden-seed evaluation harness stored in s3://redwood-golden/quantization/2025-02 for reproducibility
Integrate with existing telemetry events (trace id, model_version, profile_id) so Console rollouts show per-token deltas
Prioritize minimal runtime changes: orbiter should suggest profiles and runtime applies via existing profile activation APIs with rollback hooks
risks: False negatives: orbiter fails to catch a rare prompt class causing a customer-visible regression
Numeric nondeterminism on Hopper under heavy contention could skew calibration results
Long calibration times may block rapid rollouts; need to tune sample sizes and parallelize across shards
Overfitting to golden-suite prompts leads to optimistic confidence scores; require diverse production-sampled prompts
Operational complexity: additional moving parts (orbiter + shadow canaries) increase SRE burden
rollback_plan: Immediate automatic rollback: if live regression metric > 1.5% for two consecutive 10-minute windows, revert to previous profile and alert SRE
Manual rollback checklist in runbook with steps to disable profile, drain affected shards, and re-run orbiter analysis
Postmortem playbook: collect calibration artifacts, compare to golden-suite, and create hotfix calibration if needed
